inc-bot: PAGER -> eng-oncall: High rate of toolcall parser errors in tenant 'pemberly' (prod, VPC) since 1847623300. Error spike 4xx parsing failures, ~180/sec, ~25% of requests. Auto-incident created.

Maria C: acked. I'm oncall for next 2hrs, will take lead. First check ingress LB/edge parsing metrics and dedicated pool logs.

Ajit P: noticed similar 4xx in parser service (parser-v1) on dedicated-gpu-pool-5. Quick grep of logs:
```
2026-10-11T15:10:23.112Z ERROR parser-v1: payload validation failed tenant=pemberly req_id=abc123 error="Unexpected type for field 'user_context': object (expected string)"
2026-10-11T15:10:23.113Z WARN parser-v1: dropping request
```

Jordan S: Pemberly started a deploy ~15m before spike per deploy-bot. Could be client-side change. Maria, can you pull a sample payload?

Maria C: I have a few samples from the raw tcp dump + edge logs. Sample (redacted):
```
{
  "tool": "get_customer_profile",
  "args": {
    "user_id": "U-924",
    "user_context": { "last_seen": "2026-10-10", "segments": ["beta_users"] }
  }
}
```
Parser expected user_context as a string token with a path; now it's a nested object.

Priya R: That looks like schema drift -> client upgraded to new SDK that serializes context as JSON blob. Parser-v1 has a strict contract: user_context:string. This will cause validation fail in the protobuf/gRPC layer before runtime. Impact: realtime tool calls from Pemberly 100% hitting 4xx until we accept/transform payload.

Lucas M: Temporary mitigation options I see:
1) Apply a transformation at the ingress (edge) to coerce user_context object -> JSON string. Lightweight lua/nginx filter or API gateway transform.
2) Enable parser-v1 compatibility flag allow_extra_structs=true and reload parsers (risky, requires config rollout).
3) Route Pemberly traffic to parser-v2 (lenient) on a canary dedicated queue (requires route rule and model compatibility check).

Maria C: I can push an edge transform rule quickly. Ajit, can you validate if the lua filter is available on the VPC edge? If not, we can put a temporary reverse-proxy in front of the dedicated pool.

Ajit P: Edge in that VPC uses the customer's private NAT + our egress cell; we have an ingress proxy (edge-proxy-3) with lua enabled. I can push a short patch: if payload.args.user_context is object -> tostring(json.encode(...)) then pass through. Will test on a small sample.

Jordan S: Agree do edge transform first. Lower blast radius. Also create route rule to divert 5% traffic to parser-v2 as fallback if edge transform fails. Priya, can you coordinate the route rule?

Priya R: on it. Creating a canary route: tenant == pemberly && traffic_fraction=0.05 -> backend parser-v2-fallback. Will monitor 5xx/4xx.

Maria C: Patch ready, deploying to edge-proxy-3 (pemberly VPC) now. Patch body:
```
-- lua pseudo
local uc = body.args and body.args.user_context
if type(uc) == 'table' then
  body.args.user_context = cjson.encode(uc)
end
```
Applying as ephemeral rule (ttl 2h) and logging changes.

Ajit P: I applied patch and restarted edge-proxy-3 worker (graceful). Running synthetic test with sample payload -> success: parser accepted, toolcall completed. Live traffic shows drop in 4xx from 25% -> 3% in ~60s.

Maria C: Noted improvement. Still seeing occasional failures (old connections, retries). Priya, can you confirm canary route is live?

Priya R: Canary route pushed at 1847623570. Observability: parser-v2-fallback seeing 9% increased traffic from pemberly for 5% sampling. No errors on v2 so far.

inc-bot: Update: incident severity set to P2. Page suppressed for further pages until next update window.

Lucas M: Next steps while oncall:
- Keep edge transform for 2h, then expire.
- Leave 5% canary to parser-v2 for monitoring for 1h.
- Ask Pemberly to pin SDK rollback OR send a compatibility changelog.
- Prepare parser-v1 patch to accept JSON blob for user_context (safe deserialization) and schedule non-urgent deploy.

Maria C: I've asked pemberly-support in DMs for the release notes and whether they can roll back. They responded: "we shipped new client 2.5.0 that changed context shape; rolling back will take time, want a server-side quick fix."

Ajit P: For a more robust short-term server-side fix, we can add a permissive deserializer in parser-v1 that accepts string or any JSON object for user_context and coerces to string (json.encode). That requires a config change and a rolling restart in dedicated pool (safe but will cause ~10s tokenization jitter per worker). If customer prefers server fix, we can schedule a hotfix rollout with maintenance window in 15m.

Maria C: Pemberly asks for immediate server-side fix. They authorize a quick restart if it reduces errors. Jordan, are you comfortable with a rolling restart on dedicated-pool-5?

Jordan S: Yes, coordinate with SRE. We'll do one node at a time, drain connections, apply change, bring back. Ajit, prepare the patch and smoke test. Lucas, prepare rollback plan and metrics alarms.

Ajit P: Patch prepared: set user_context_accepts_object=true by default for tenant pemberly (scoped toggle). Code snippet:
```
if type(payload.args.user_context) != 'string' then
  payload.args.user_context = json.encode(payload.args.user_context)
end
```
I'll deploy to one worker, run synthetic tests.

Maria C: Deploy started 1847623720 -> node-3 drained, applied patch, restarted worker. Smoke tests pass. Live metrics for node-3 show no regressions.

Priya R: Canary observe: after one node updated, 4xx reduced to 1.2% across tenant. Keep rolling.

Maria C: Rolling through other nodes. ETA ~10m. Logging all changes in incident doc.

inc-bot: Note: manual change detected on parser-v1 dedicated pool for tenant=pemberly. Please add IR ticket reference and follow postmortem cadence.

Lucas M: After full roll, we should still keep edge transform for 30 minutes then remove. Also add a contract test in our CI that runs against sample payloads from customers with schema variants.

Maria C: Roll complete at 1847623950. Overall 4xx down to baseline 0.2%. Customer reports traffic normal.

pemberly-support: Thanks to the team, this unblocked our production traffic. We'll revert SDK change in next patch to align with API contract. We'll also provide a sample schema to Redwood PD team.

Jordan S: Handoff for next oncall (Lucas M):
- Incident summary: schema drift in pemberly toolcall user_context field caused parser-v1 validation errors. Immediate mitigations: edge lua transform + parser-v1 scoped toggle + 5% canary to parser-v2.
- Remaining actions: follow up patch to parser-v1 in source repo (PR opened by Ajit), add e2e contract tests, coordinate with Pemberly for SDK changelog, file PIR and schedule postmortem.
- Links: incident doc /incidents/1847623456, pager history, PR-5823 (patch), metrics dashboard link (internal).
- Oncall notes: watch for regression in 1h and any increase in latency on parser-v1 nodes (tokenization CPU).

Lucas M: ack. I'll take next shift. Adding action items to my queue: ensure PR passes canary and schedule a maintenance window for a permanent fix next week.

Maria C: Thanks team. I'll create the postmortem stub and collect customer payload samples. Closing active page, will keep monitoring for 2h.

inc-bot: Incident state -> MONITORING. P2 -> closed in 2h if no regression.

Jordan S: Closing notes: recommend product/standing meeting with Pemberly to agree on API contract and upgrade cadence, and add a feature flag to surface incompatible SDKs earlier (warning headers).

Lucas M: leaving a followup todo: implement schema-lint in onboarding pipeline for enterprise tenants to avoid silent breakage.

Maria C: End of thread.
